title: A million buckets
summary: A huge chip of programmed buckets, sipping power while it runs.

cards.text:
The links are written in ahead of time.
The chip’s job is to run, not to learn on the fly.

question.prompt: This 2014 chip updates its own links while it runs.
question.why: Weights are programmed. Learning happened elsewhere.
question.simpler: That is a specification, not a flaw in an inference machine.

question.why: Power without the workload is not a result.
question.simpler: Keep the number next to the task.

recall.question: Does TrueNorth learn its synapses on the chip while it runs?
recall.answer: No. They are programmed ahead of time.

deeper.note: Merolla and colleagues, Science 2014. 4096 cores, a million neurons, 256 million synapses. The milliwatts are the vision demo.

paper.title: A million spiking-neuron integrated circuit with a scalable communication network and interface
paper.section: The core, the tiling, and the power of the vision demonstration.

terms.definition: A tile of axons, neurons, and synapses that runs a fixed spiking network. TrueNorth is the 2014 example.
